statement.p: And now we can use the geometric series expression to get \frac{1}{(8+x)}=\frac{1}{8}\cdot \frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{8}x}=\frac{1}{8}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{-1}{8}x\right)^n=\frac{1}{8}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(\frac{-1}{8}\right)^nx^n
Bringing the coefficient inside the sum means that \frac{1}{(8+x)}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{8^{n+1}}x^n
